turns.assessment: The impact is confined to services whose working path uses och75 between S04 and S14; services sharing the S10-S21-S08-S04 portion but not och75 remained healthy. Both och75 endpoints recorded only one errored second, while protected services briefly switched and restored, indicating a short bidirectional disturbance rather than a persistent equipment failure. The absence of reported power, OSNR, DGD, or equipment-monitor changes most strongly favors a fast SOP transient on one of the fibre spans, potentially affecting both fibres in the cable, but the evidence does not identify which span.

proposals.rationale: A millisecond-scale polarization transient can produce isolated errored seconds and protection switching without a power alarm or sampled PM change. It fits the transient errors on och75 and the common S04-S14 dependency; a physical disturbance could affect the paired reverse-direction fibre observed at O43.

Brief handling or movement of a span could disturb both fibres and explain the short service event, but its expected power excursion should have been more likely to appear in optical monitoring than the observed no-change pattern.

A channel-specific filter penalty could affect och75 without disturbing unrelated channels, but it would normally persist and does not naturally explain the similarly brief reverse-direction error at O43.

score.why: truth not in the reported set
